sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca saṃkalpadaṃśamaśakaṃ śokaharṣahimātapam mohāndhakāratimiraṃ lobhavyālasarīsṛpam
english: The brāhmaṇa said: Its gnats and mosquitoes are the cravings of the will; its cold and heat are grief and elation; its blinding gloom is delusion; its creeping serpents are the snakes of greed —

sanskrit: viṣayaikātyayādhvānaṃ kāmakrodhavirodhakam tad atītya mahādurgaṃ praviṣṭo 'smi mahad vanam
english: its road that must be crossed leads through the objects of sense alone; its hostile barriers are desire and anger. Having passed through that great and trackless waste, I have entered a vast forest.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇy uvāca kva tad vanaṃ mahāprājña ke vṛkṣāḥ saritaś ca kāḥ girayaḥ parvatāś caiva kiyaty adhvani tad vanam
english: The brāhmaṇa's wife said: Where is that forest, O man of great wisdom? What are its trees, what its streams, what its hills and mountains, and at what distance does that forest lie?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca na tad asti pṛthagbhāve kiṃ cid anyat tataḥ samam na tad asty apṛthagbhāve kiṃ cid dūrataraṃ tataḥ
english: The brāhmaṇa said: In the realm of separateness there is nothing else equal to it; in the realm of non-separateness there is nothing more remote than it.

sanskrit: tasmād dhrasvataraṃ nāsti na tato 'sti bṛhattaram nāsti tasmād duḥkhataraṃ nāsty anyat tatsamaṃ sukham
english: There is nothing shorter than it, and nothing greater than it; there is nothing more sorrowful than it, and no joy that equals it.

sanskrit: na tat praviśya śocanti na prahṛṣyanti ca dvijāḥ na ca bibhyati keṣāṃ cit tebhyo bibhyati ke ca na
english: Having entered it, the twice-born neither grieve nor rejoice; they fear nothing from any quarter, and there are those who do not fear them.

sanskrit: tasmin vane sapta mahādrumāś ca; phalāni saptātithayaś ca sapta saptāśramāḥ sapta samādhayaś ca; dīkṣāś ca saptaitad araṇyarūpam
english: In that forest are seven great trees, seven fruits, seven guests, seven hermitages, seven kinds of meditation, and seven consecrations — such is the form of that wilderness.

sanskrit: pañcavarṇāni divyāni puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca sṛjantaḥ pādapās tatra vyāpya tiṣṭhanti tad vanam
english: Trees putting forth divine flowers and fruits of five colors stand pervading that forest.

sanskrit: suvarṇāni dvivarṇāni puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca sṛjantaḥ pādapās tatra vyāpya tiṣṭhanti tad vanam
english: Trees putting forth flowers and fruits of fair hue and of two colors stand pervading that forest.

sanskrit: caturvarṇāni divyāni puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca sṛjantaḥ pādapās tatra vyāpya tiṣṭhanti tad vanam
english: Trees putting forth divine flowers and fruits of four colors stand pervading that forest.

sanskrit: śaṃkarāṇi trivarṇāni puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca sṛjantaḥ pādapās tatra vyāpya tiṣṭhanti tad vanam
english: Trees putting forth auspicious flowers and fruits of three colors stand pervading that forest.

sanskrit: surabhīṇy ekavarṇāni puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca sṛjantaḥ pādapās tatra vyāpya tiṣṭhanti tad vanam
english: Trees putting forth fragrant flowers and fruits of a single color stand pervading that forest.

sanskrit: bahūny avyaktavarṇāni puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca visṛjantau mahāvṛkṣau tad vanaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhataḥ
english: And two great trees, putting forth many flowers and fruits of indistinct color, stand pervading that forest.

sanskrit: eko hy agniḥ sumanā brāhmaṇo 'tra; pañcendriyāṇi samidhaś cātra santi tebhyo mokṣāḥ sapta bhavanti dīkṣā; guṇāḥ phalāny atithayaḥ phalāśāḥ
english: Here is one fire, the gladdened brāhmaṇa; here are the five senses for its kindling-sticks; from these arise the seven releases that are the consecrations; the qualities are the fruits, and the guests are those who long for the fruits.

sanskrit: ātithyaṃ pratigṛhṇanti tatra sapta maharṣayaḥ arciteṣu pralīneṣu teṣv anyad rocate vanam
english: There the seven great seers accept the hospitality; and when they, being honored, have dissolved away, another forest shines forth.

sanskrit: pratijñāvṛkṣam aphalaṃ śānticchāyāsamanvitam jñānāśrayaṃ tṛptitoyam antaḥkṣetrajñabhāskaram
english: There stands the tree of resolve, fruitless, attended by the shade of peace, the refuge of knowledge, watered by contentment, and lit within by the sun that is the Knower of the field.

sanskrit: ye 'dhigacchanti tat santas teṣāṃ nāsti bhayaṃ punaḥ ūrdhvaṃ cāvāk ca tiryak ca tasya nānto 'dhigamyate
english: For the good who attain that, there is no further fear; above, below, and across, its limit cannot be reached.

sanskrit: sapta striyas tatra vasanti sadyo; avāṅmukhā bhānumatyo janitryaḥ ūrdhvaṃ rasānāṃ dadate prajābhyaḥ; sarvān yathā sarvam anityatāṃ ca
english: Seven women dwell there ever-present, downward-faced, radiant, and life-bearing; they bestow upon creatures the upward essences of all things, and likewise all impermanence.

sanskrit: tatraiva pratitiṣṭhanti punas tatrodayanti ca sapta saptarṣayaḥ siddhā vasiṣṭhapramukhāḥ saha
english: There abide and from there again arise the seven groups of seven seers, the perfected ones, with Vasiṣṭha at their head.

sanskrit: yaśo varco bhagaś caiva vijayaḥ siddhitejasī evam evānuvartante sapta jyotīṃṣi bhāskaram
english: Glory, splendor, fortune, victory, accomplishment, and brilliance — even so do seven lights attend upon the sun.

sanskrit: girayaḥ parvatāś caiva santi tatra samāsataḥ nadyaś ca sarito vāri vahantyo brahmasaṃbhavam
english: There too, in brief, are hills and mountains, and rivers and streams bearing waters sprung from Brahman.

sanskrit: nadīnāṃ saṃgamas tatra vaitānaḥ samupahvare svātmatṛptā yato yānti sākṣād dāntāḥ pitāmaham
english: There, in a secret place, is the confluence of the rivers, the sacred fire; from there those who are content in the Self, the self-restrained, go directly to the Grandfather.

sanskrit: kṛśāśāḥ suvratāśāś ca tapasā dagdhakilbiṣāḥ ātmany ātmānam āveśya brahmāṇaṃ samupāsate
english: With desires made lean and hopes turned to good vows, their sins burnt away by austerity, they merge the self in the Self and worship Brahman.

sanskrit: ṛcam apy atra śaṃsanti vidyāraṇyavido janāḥ tad araṇyam abhipretya yathādhīram ajāyata
english: Here too the people learned in the forest of knowledge recite a hymn that, intending that wilderness, arose in measure with steadfastness.

sanskrit: etad etādṛśaṃ divyam araṇyaṃ brāhmaṇā viduḥ viditvā cānvatiṣṭhanta kṣetrajñenānudarśitam
english: Such, of this nature, is the divine wilderness that the brāhmaṇas know; and having known it, as shown to them by the Knower of the field, they have lived in accordance with it.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca gandhān na jighrāmi rasān na vedmi; rūpaṃ na paśyāmi na ca spṛśāmi na cāpi śabdān vividhāñ śṛṇomi; na cāpi saṃkalpam upaimi kiṃ cit
english: The brāhmaṇa said: I do not smell odors, I do not taste flavors, I do not see form, nor do I touch, nor do I hear the manifold sounds, nor do I entertain any willful thought at all.

sanskrit: arthān iṣṭān kāmayate svabhāvaḥ; sarvān dveṣyān pradviṣate svabhāvaḥ kāmadveṣāv udbhavataḥ svabhāvāt; prāṇāpānau jantudehān niveśya
english: It is one's own nature that desires the wished-for objects, one's own nature that hates all that is hateful; desire and hatred spring up from nature, having lodged the in-breath and out-breath within the bodies of creatures.

sanskrit: tebhyaś cānyāṃs teṣv anityāṃś ca bhāvān; bhūtātmānaṃ lakṣayeyaṃ śarīre tasmiṃs tiṣṭhan nāsmi śakyaḥ kathaṃ cit; kāmakrodhābhyāṃ jarayā mṛtyunā ca
english: From these and other states, impermanent within them, I would mark out the elemental self within the body; and dwelling in that, I cannot in any way be assailed by desire and anger, by old age, or by death.

sanskrit: akāmayānasya ca sarvakāmān; avidviṣāṇasya ca sarvadoṣān na me svabhāveṣu bhavanti lepās; toyasya bindor iva puṣkareṣu
english: For one who craves none of the objects of desire and hates none of the faults, no stains cling to me amid the modes of nature, as a drop of water does not cling to the lotus leaves.

sanskrit: nityasya caitasya bhavanti nityā; nirīkṣamāṇasya bahūn svabhāvān na sajjate karmasu bhogajālaṃ; divīva sūryasya mayūkhajālam
english: For this eternal one, who beholds the many modes of nature, the eternal things remain; the net of enjoyment does not cling to him in his actions, as in the sky the net of the sun's rays does not cling.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam adhvaryuyatisaṃvādaṃ taṃ nibodha yaśasvini
english: On this they recite an ancient tale, the dialogue of the adhvaryu priest and the ascetic; mark it well, O illustrious lady.

sanskrit: prokṣyamāṇaṃ paśuṃ dṛṣṭvā yajñakarmaṇy athābravīt yatir adhvaryum āsīno hiṃseyam iti kutsayan
english: Seeing the sacrificial victim being sprinkled in the rite, the seated ascetic spoke to the adhvaryu, condemning it: 'This is violence.'

sanskrit: tam adhvaryuḥ pratyuvāca nāyaṃ chāgo vinaśyati śreyasā yokṣyate jantur yadi śrutir iyaṃ tathā
english: To him the adhvaryu replied: This goat does not perish; the creature will be joined to a higher good, if this Vedic teaching is true.

sanskrit: yo hy asya pārthivo bhāgaḥ pṛthivīṃ sa gamiṣyati yad asya vārijaṃ kiṃ cid apas tat pratipadyate
english: For that part of it which is earthly will go to the earth, and whatever in it is born of water returns to the waters.

sanskrit: sūryaṃ cakṣur diśaḥ śrotre prāṇo 'sya divam eva ca āgame vartamānasya na me doṣo 'sti kaś cana
english: Its eye goes to the sun, its hearing to the quarters, its breath to the very sky; for me, who act in keeping with sacred tradition, there is no fault at all.

sanskrit: yatir uvāca prāṇair viyoge chāgasya yadi śreyaḥ prapaśyasi chāgārthe vartate yajño bhavataḥ kiṃ prayojanam
english: The ascetic said: If you foresee a higher good for the goat in its parting from life, then the sacrifice exists for the goat's sake — what use is it to you?

sanskrit: anu tvā manyatāṃ mātā pitā bhrātā sakhāpi ca mantrayasvainam unnīya paravantaṃ viśeṣataḥ
english: Let its mother, father, brother, and friend give you their consent; take counsel with them, having first brought up the creature — especially since it belongs to others.

sanskrit: ya evam anumanyeraṃs tān bhavān praṣṭum arhati teṣām anumataṃ śrutvā śakyā kartuṃ vicāraṇā
english: You ought to ask those who would thus give consent; and having heard their assent, the deliberation can be carried out.

sanskrit: prāṇā apy asya chāgasya prāpitās te svayoniṣu śarīraṃ kevalaṃ śiṣṭaṃ niśceṣṭam iti me matiḥ
english: As for the life-breaths of this goat, they have been led back to their own sources; only the body remains, motionless — so it is my view.

sanskrit: indhanasya tu tulyena śarīreṇa vicetasā hiṃsā nirveṣṭukāmānām indhanaṃ paśusaṃjñitam
english: But for those who wish to be free of violence, the body, devoid of consciousness and like mere fuel, is fuel that goes by the name of victim.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā sarvadharmāṇām iti vṛddhānuśāsanam yad ahiṃsraṃ bhavet karma tat kāryam iti vidmahe
english: 'Non-violence is the highest of all duties' — such is the teaching of the elders; and we hold that whatever action is free of harm is the action to be done.

sanskrit: ahiṃseti pratijñeyaṃ yadi vakṣyāmy ataḥ param śakyaṃ bahuvidhaṃ vaktuṃ bhavataḥ kāryadūṣaṇam
english: 'Non-violence' must be the vow declared; and if I were to speak further than this, much could be said in many ways to fault your performance.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā sarvabhūtānāṃ nityam asmāsu rocate pratyakṣataḥ sādhayāmo na parokṣam upāsmahe
english: Non-violence toward all beings is what ever pleases us; we accomplish it before our very eyes — we do not serve what is unseen.

sanskrit: adhvaryur uvāca bhūmer gandhaguṇān bhuṅkṣe pibasy āpomayān rasān jyotiṣāṃ paśyase rūpaṃ spṛśasy anilajān guṇān
english: The adhvaryu said: You enjoy the quality of smell that belongs to earth, you drink the watery flavors, you see the form that belongs to the luminaries, you touch the qualities born of air,

sanskrit: śṛṇoṣy ākāśajaṃ śabdaṃ manasā manyase matim sarvāṇy etāni bhūtāni prāṇā iti ca manyase
english: you hear the sound born of space, and with the mind you conceive thought; and you regard all these elements as living beings.

sanskrit: prāṇādāne ca nityo 'si hiṃsāyāṃ vartate bhavān nāsti ceṣṭā vinā hiṃsāṃ kiṃ vā tvaṃ manyase dvija
english: You are constantly taking life away, and so you live in violence; there is no activity without harm. Or what do you think, O twice-born?

sanskrit: yatir uvāca akṣaraṃ ca kṣaraṃ caiva dvaidhībhāvo 'yam ātmanaḥ akṣaraṃ tatra sadbhāvaḥ svabhāvaḥ kṣara ucyate
english: The ascetic said: The imperishable and the perishable — this is the twofold being of the Self; therein the imperishable is true being, while one's own nature is called the perishable.

sanskrit: prāṇo jihvā manaḥ sattvaṃ svabhāvo rajasā saha bhāvair etair vimuktasya nirdvaṃdvasya nirāśiṣaḥ
english: Breath, tongue, mind, and goodness — this nature, together with passion: for one freed from these states, free of the pairs of opposites and of all craving,

sanskrit: samasya sarvabhūteṣu nirmamasya jitātmanaḥ samantāt parimuktasya na bhayaṃ vidyate kva cit
english: who is equal toward all beings, free of possessiveness, self-conquered, and wholly liberated, no fear exists anywhere.

sanskrit: adhvaryur uvāca sadbhir eveha saṃvāsaḥ kāryo matimatāṃ vara bhavato hi mataṃ śrutvā pratibhāti matir mama
english: The adhvaryu said: Surely fellowship is to be kept here only with the good, O best of the wise; for, having heard your view, my own understanding grows clear.

sanskrit: bhagavan bhagavadbuddhyā pratibuddho bravīmy aham mataṃ mantuṃ kratuṃ kartuṃ nāparādho 'sti me dvija
english: Reverend one, awakened by your reverend understanding, I declare: in holding this view and in performing the sacrifice, there is no offense in me, O twice-born.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca upapattyā yatis tūṣṇīṃ vartamānas tataḥ param adhvaryur api nirmohaḥ pracacāra mahāmakhe
english: The brāhmaṇa said: Thereafter the ascetic, content with this reasoning, abode in silence; and the adhvaryu too, his delusion gone, proceeded with the great sacrifice.

sanskrit: evam etādṛśaṃ mokṣaṃ susūkṣmaṃ brāhmaṇā viduḥ viditvā cānutiṣṭhanti kṣetrajñenānudarśinā
english: Thus do the brāhmaṇas know this most subtle liberation; and having known it, they live by it, as shown by the Knower of the field.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam kārtavīryasya saṃvādaṃ samudrasya ca bhāmini
english: The brāhmaṇa said: On this too they recite an ancient tale, the dialogue of Kārtavīrya and the Ocean, O lovely lady.

sanskrit: kārtavīryārjuno nāma rājā bāhusahasravān yena sāgaraparyantā dhanuṣā nirjitā mahī
english: There was a king named Kārtavīrya Arjuna, possessed of a thousand arms, by whom, with his bow, the earth to its ocean-shores was conquered.

sanskrit: sa kadā cit samudrānte vicaran baladarpitaḥ avākirac charaśataiḥ samudram iti naḥ śrutam
english: Once, roaming along the ocean's edge, proud of his strength, he showered the sea with hundreds of arrows — so we have heard.

sanskrit: taṃ samudro namaskṛtya kṛtāñjalir uvāca ha mā muñca vīra nārācān brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te
english: The Ocean bowed to him and, with hands joined in reverence, said: Do not loose your iron shafts, O hero; tell me, what shall I do for you?

sanskrit: madāśrayāṇi bhūtāni tvadvisṛṣṭair maheṣubhiḥ vadhyante rājaśārdūla tebhyo dehy abhayaṃ vibho
english: The creatures that take refuge in me are being slain by your mighty arrows, O tiger among kings; grant them safety, O lord.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca matsamo yadi saṃgrāme śarāsanadharaḥ kva cit vidyate taṃ mamācakṣva yaḥ samāsīta māṃ mṛdhe
english: Arjuna said: If anywhere there exists a bearer of the bow equal to me in battle, point him out to me — one who could stand against me in the fray.

sanskrit: samudra uvāca maharṣir jamadagnis te yadi rājan pariśrutaḥ tasya putras tavātithyaṃ yathāvat kartum arhati
english: The Ocean said: If, O king, the great seer Jamadagni is known to you, his son is able to offer you fitting hospitality.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājā prayayau krodhena mahatā vṛtaḥ sa tam āśramam āgamya rāmam evānvapadyata
english: Then the king set out, wrapped in great wrath; and coming to that hermitage, he sought out Rāma himself.

sanskrit: sa rāmapratikūlāni cakāra saha bandhubhiḥ āyāsaṃ janayām āsa rāmasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Together with his kinsmen he did deeds hostile to Rāma, and he brought distress upon the great-souled Rāma.

sanskrit: tatas tejaḥ prajajvāla rāmasyāmitatejasaḥ pradahad ripusainyāni tadā kamalalocane
english: Then the fiery power of Rāma of boundless splendor blazed forth, consuming the armies of the foe, O lotus-eyed one.

sanskrit: tataḥ paraśum ādāya sa taṃ bāhusahasriṇam ciccheda sahasā rāmo bāhuśākham iva drumam
english: Then, taking up his axe, Rāma swiftly cut down that thousand-armed king, as one lops a tree of its branching boughs.

sanskrit: taṃ hataṃ patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sametāḥ sarvabāndhavāḥ asīn ādāya śaktīś ca bhārgavaṃ paryavārayan
english: Seeing him slain and fallen, all his kinsmen gathered, and taking up their swords and spears, surrounded the descendant of Bhṛgu.

sanskrit: rāmo 'pi dhanur ādāya ratham āruhya satvaraḥ visṛjañ śaravarṣāṇi vyadhamat pārthivaṃ balam
english: Rāma too, taking up his bow and swiftly mounting his chariot, loosed showers of arrows and scattered the host of those kings.

sanskrit: tatas tu kṣatriyāḥ ke cij jamadagniṃ nihatya ca viviśur giridurgāṇi mṛgāḥ siṃhārditā iva
english: Then certain warriors, having slain Jamadagni, fled into the mountain fastnesses, like deer harried by a lion.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ svavihitaṃ karma tadbhayān nānutiṣṭhatām prajā vṛṣalatāṃ prāptā brāhmaṇānām adarśanāt
english: Out of that fear they no longer performed the duties ordained for them, and their offspring, for want of the sight of brāhmaṇas, fell to the condition of outcastes.

sanskrit: ta ete dramiḍāḥ kāśāḥ puṇḍrāś ca śabaraiḥ saha vṛṣalatvaṃ parigatā vyutthānāt kṣatradharmataḥ
english: These are the Draviḍas, the Kāśas, and the Puṇḍras, together with the Śabaras, who through their lapse from the warrior's duty came to the state of outcastes.

sanskrit: tatas tu hatavīrāsu kṣatriyāsu punaḥ punaḥ dvijair utpāditaṃ kṣatraṃ jāmadagnyo nyakṛntata
english: Then, when the warrior race had been stripped of its heroes again and again, the warriors begotten anew upon them by the brāhmaṇas were cut down by the son of Jamadagni.

sanskrit: ekaviṃśatimedhānte rāmaṃ vāg aśarīriṇī divyā provāca madhurā sarvalokapariśrutā
english: At the end of the twenty-first slaughter, a bodiless voice, divine and sweet, heard throughout all the worlds, spoke to Rāma:

sanskrit: rāma rāma nivartasva kaṃ guṇaṃ tāta paśyasi kṣatrabandhūn imān prāṇair viprayojya punaḥ punaḥ
english: Rāma, Rāma, desist! What merit, dear son, do you see in robbing these wretched warriors of their lives again and again?

sanskrit: tathaiva taṃ mahātmānam ṛcīkapramukhās tadā pitāmahā mahābhāga nivartasvety athābruvan
english: Likewise the forefathers, with Ṛcīka at their head, then said to that great-souled one, O blessed lady: Desist!

sanskrit: pitur vadham amṛṣyaṃs tu rāmaḥ provāca tān ṛṣīn nārhantīha bhavanto māṃ nivārayitum ity uta
english: But Rāma, unable to bear his father's slaying, said to those seers: Your honors have no right to restrain me here.

sanskrit: pitara ūcuḥ nārhase kṣatrabandhūṃs tvaṃ nihantuṃ jayatāṃ vara na hi yuktaṃ tvayā hantuṃ brāhmaṇena satā nṛpān
english: The forefathers said: You ought not to slay these warriors, O best of the victorious; for it is not fitting that you, a true brāhmaṇa, should kill kings.

sanskrit: pitara ūcuḥ atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam śrutvā ca tat tathā kāryaṃ bhavatā dvijasattama
english: The forefathers said: On this too they recite an ancient tale; having heard it, you must act accordingly, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: alarko nāma rājarṣir abhavat sumahātapāḥ dharmajñaḥ satyasaṃdhaś ca mahātmā sumahāvrataḥ
english: There was a royal seer named Alarka, of mighty austerity, knower of duty, true to his word, great-souled, and firm in great vows.

sanskrit: sa sāgarāntāṃ dhanuṣā vinirjitya mahīm imām kṛtvā suduṣkaraṃ karma manaḥ sūkṣme samādadhe
english: Having conquered this earth to its ocean-shores with his bow, and having done that most arduous deed, he fixed his mind upon the subtle.

sanskrit: sthitasya vṛkṣamūle 'tha tasya cintā babhūva ha utsṛjya sumahad rājyaṃ sūkṣmaṃ prati mahāmate
english: As he sat at the foot of a tree, this thought arose in him — having renounced his vast kingdom — concerning the subtle, O great-minded one:

sanskrit: alarka uvāca manaso me balaṃ jātaṃ mano jitvā dhruvo jayaḥ anyatra bāṇān asyāmi śatrubhiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: Alarka said: The power of my mind has grown great; once the mind is conquered, victory is assured. Beset by foes, I shall loose my arrows elsewhere.
